items.name: 〜られる・〜える (可能形)
items.summary: The potential form expresses ability or possibility. Ru-verbs take られる; u-verbs shift the final sound to the e-row + る (話す→話せる).

items.name: 〜ようにする
items.gloss: make an effort to / try to make a habit of
items.summary: The dictionary or ない-form + ようにする expresses making a conscious effort to do (or avoid) something, often habitually — distinct from 〜ようになる, which describes a change that happens on its own.

items.name: 〜のに（使う）
items.gloss: for ~ing, in order to (before a verb of use/need)
items.summary: The dictionary form + のに, followed by a verb like 使う or an expression like 必要だ／時間がかかる, states the purpose something is used for or the cost of doing it — a different のに from the concessive 'even though' sense.

items.name: 〜てくる・〜ていく
items.gloss: a change coming this way / a change going on from here
items.summary: て-form + くる frames a change as having led up to now (toward the speaker); て-form + いく frames a change as continuing on from now (away from the speaker) — the same forms used for literal coming and going, extended to describe change over time.

items.name: 〜しか〜ない
items.summary: しか, paired with a negative predicate, narrows something down to the one thing named — nothing else qualifies (only …). With an animate subject the negative is いない, not ない.
